summary.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue rose 13.5% to INR896 crore and PAT grew 164% to INR40.69 crore, but Q4 EBITDA margin fell to 6.84% on the Middle East cost shock.
summary.overview: FY26 was a record year: consolidated revenue grew 13.5% YoY to above INR896 crore, EBITDA rose 49.21% to INR92.21 crore at a 10.29% margin, and PAT rose 164% to INR40.69 crore. Q4 FY26 revenue was INR228.74 crore (up 20.45% QoQ, 9% YoY), but EBITDA margin compressed to 6.84% (INR15.64 crore) as freight, energy and raw material costs spiked after the Middle East conflict. The alu-zinc line was commissioned in late December 2025 and is ramping up in phases. Management said new contracts since April 2026 pass through the full incremental cost, and that H1 FY27 margins should recover meaningfully.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR73,622 per ton in FY25
YoY margin softer; no comparative figure given

segments.name: Galvanized and alu-zinc coated steel
segments.commentary: FY26 production was 1,03,036 MT, up 2.21% YoY. Alu-zinc capacity rose from 1,32,000 MT to 1,80,000 MT (+36%) after the line was commissioned in late December 2025.

segments.name: Pre-painted steel
segments.commentary: FY26 production grew 12.78% YoY to 83,594 MT. It made up 80% of quantities sold in FY26, up from 74% in FY25.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: FY26 export tonnage was a record 66,172 MT, up 110% YoY from 31,453 MT. Exports reached 68.21% of revenue, up from 39.21% in FY25.

guidance_outlook: Second colour coating line (+1,50,000 MT, total colour capacity 86,000 to 2,36,000 MT) targeted for July 2026; capex about INR65 crore. Management referred to Q2 FY27 commissioning.
7 MW captive solar plant in Gujarat, capex INR30 crore, targeted July 2026. It should offset 50-55% of grid power and save INR7-7.5 crore per year; about half that benefit is expected in FY27.
Incremental FY27 revenue from the new colour coating line estimated at INR300-500 crore over FY26 levels, depending on ramp-up.
Alu-zinc line expected to reach 80-85% utilisation within FY27, with H2 FY27 well above H1. Management said 60-65% utilisation was already achieved.
Sustainable EBITDA margin guided at 10-12%. Management said new orders pass through the full cost increase, and H1 FY27 margin recovery should be meaningful, assuming no further escalation.
Cold rolling mill backward integration targeted within FY28, with no date fixed and financing not yet tied up. Management said it would not breach 2x debt-equity and aims for 1x-1.5x.

Long-term vision of 3x revenue and profitability by FY29, driven by capacity of 0.36 million tons, cold rolling and further alu-zinc expansion. Management said projects are targeted to earn ROCE above 20%.
capex_capacity: Alu-zinc line commissioned end-December 2025, lifting capacity from 1,32,000 MT to 1,80,000 MT; ramp-up is phased and incremental.
Second colour coating line (+1,50,000 MT, Mas Rollpro) in advanced erection and commissioning, completion targeted July 2026, INR65 crore.
7 MW captive solar project (Prozeal Green Energy, Gujarat), INR30 crore, commissioning targeted July 2026.

Planned cold rolling complex (backward integration) targeted within FY28; assumed 3,60,000 MT cold rolling, a second alu-zinc plant and 2,36,000 MT pre-painted capacity. Assumed 80-85% utilisation implies INR2,500-2,700 crore revenue, per management's hypothetical math.
Salesforce finalised as preferred CRM platform.
demand_pricing: Management said the order book is INR350-400 crore, mostly from export customers, and that long-term customers are ordering in advance to build buffers.
Alu-zinc premium over galvanized is about INR3,000-5,000 per ton on price realisation (ballpark, depends on gauge and coating grammage).
Pass-through: management said all new contracts since April 2026 pass through the full incremental energy, raw material, consumables and freight costs.
Management expects a cost-driven lag of at most one to two months when input costs fall, and said margins should improve versus Q4.
Management said regular, long-term customers account for upwards of 70% of revenue, and new customers are added every quarter.
New alu-zinc export markets: South and Central America and the Caribbean are the target regions, with a slight premium over current markets. The company has no US exposure.
Management said freight rates rose about 100% QoQ, LPG/propane prices spiked about 200% within a fortnight, and key raw material and consumable costs rose 50-75%.

qa_highlights.question: Total capex outlay till FY28 and how it is funded?
qa_highlights.answer: The second colour coating line is about INR65 crore and the solar plant INR30 crore, both commissioning in Q2 FY27. Funding is a mix of debt from PSU banks and equity from the last fund raise.

qa_highlights.question: Will demand keep pace with 2-3x capacity expansion, given export concentration?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports rose from about 20-25% of revenue three to four years ago to about 70% now. Management expects export growth to slow from 100% but still grow in revenue and tonnage.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainable EBITDA upside from alu-zinc: pricing power or cost efficiency?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number. It said alu-zinc is structurally more profitable on cost and price, and the premium depends on cost, yield and utilisation (internal) plus demand and competition (external).

qa_highlights.question: Who will pay for the new cold rolling complex, and what are the ROCE and IRR?
qa_highlights.answer: Cold rolling is targeted within FY28, with no date, financing or supplier selection yet. Management said projects target ROCE above 20%, but this is not yet modelled.

qa_highlights.question: Will the elevated raw material cost persist into Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Costs remain high. New contracts since April pass through the full incremental cost, so management expects margins to be drastically better than Q4 FY26. A cost decline would bring a lag of about one to two months.

qa_highlights.question: Leverage threshold and future fund raising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will not breach 2x debt-equity and aims for 1x-1.5x. No fund raise is planned now; the cold rolling mill would be next, with fund raising undecided.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 revenue estimate from alu-zinc plus the new colour line?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated INR300-500 crore of incremental FY27 revenue over FY26 from the new colour line and higher alu-zinc utilisation. It did not confirm a total FY27 figure.

qa_highlights.question: Alu-zinc premium over galvanized?
qa_highlights.answer: Ballpark of INR3,000-5,000 per ton on price realisation, depending on specification, gauge and coating grammage.

risks_watch: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin of 6.84% reflects the energy and raw material shock; the H1 FY27 margin recovery depends on pass-through holding and the conflict not escalating further.
Ramp-up of the alu-zinc line (60-65% utilisation today) and the colour coating line (targeted July 2026) could slip, which would delay the INR300-500 crore revenue uplift.
Export concentration (about 68-70% of revenue) and the slowing export growth rate expected by management.
Cold rolling backward integration (FY28) is unfunded and undated, with a possible fund raise still undecided.
Management's 3x revenue and profitability by FY29 target is conditional on several projects and external factors.
Q4 PAT margin of 2.35% is thin, and an input-cost reversal could create a lag in pass-through.
The call was disrupted by a poor-quality line and an unanswered question, so some Q&A detail may be incomplete.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the full-year record and forward capacity, but openly cautious on Q4 margins and Q1 FY27 costs. Management was evasive on ROCE, IRR, EBITDA-per-ton premium and FY27 revenue totals, citing hypothetical assumptions.
key_quotes: We are successfully able to pass through the entire impact of the incremental costs to our customers, and we have strong visibility of EBITDA earnings for the quarters yet to unfold.
We will definitely not breach a level of 2x, and we'll strive to actually be anywhere in the range of between 1x to 1.5x.
And as on date, we are already using upwards of 60%, 65% capacity utilization on the new alu-zinc line, and most of it is going to existing customers.
